title: Of the Perseverance of the Saints
subtitle: Those whom God has accepted, effectually called, and sanctified shall certainly persevere to the end and be eternally saved.

paragraphs.text: Those whom God has accepted in the Beloved, effectually called, and sanctified by his Spirit, and to whom he has given the precious faith of his elect, can neither totally nor finally fall from the state of grace. They will certainly persevere in grace to the end and be eternally saved, because the gifts and callings of God are without repentance. He therefore continues to beget and nourish in them faith, repentance, love, joy, hope, and all the graces of the Spirit, unto immortality. Many storms and floods may rise and beat against them, but they shall never be torn from the foundation and rock to which faith has fastened them. The felt sense of God's light and love may, through unbelief and the temptations of Satan, be clouded and obscured from them for a time; yet he himself remains the same, and they shall surely be kept by the power of God unto salvation — there to enjoy the inheritance he purchased for them — for they are engraved upon the palms of his hands, and their names have been written in the book of life from all eternity.

The perseverance of the saints does not depend on their own free will, but on the unchangeable decree of election, flowing from the free and unchanging love of God the Father, the efficacy of the merit and intercession of Jesus Christ and his union with them, the oath of God, the abiding of his Spirit and seed of God within them, and the nature of the covenant of grace. It is from all these that both the certainty and infallibility of their perseverance arise.

Yet true believers may, through the temptations of Satan and the world, the prevailing of corruption that still remains in them, and the neglect of the means appointed for their preservation, fall into grievous sins and continue in them for a time. By this they incur God's displeasure and grieve his Holy Spirit; their graces and comforts are weakened; their hearts are hardened, and their consciences wounded; they hurt and scandalize others, and bring temporal judgments upon themselves. Nevertheless, they shall renew their repentance and be preserved through faith in Christ Jesus to the end.
